name: diabetes in pregnancy overview
title: Diabetes in pregnancy split by when the high glucose starts: pre-existing type 1 or 2 diabetes (planned before conception, then managed trimester by trimester) causes malformations, while gestational diabetes found on the 24-28 week screen does not; a gestational diabetes that does not clear after delivery was type 2 all along; each column gives risks, numbered checks and treatment in order

root.title: Diabetes in pregnancy: was the glucose high BEFORE organogenesis?
lines: organogenesis runs weeks 3–16, often before she knows she is pregnant
glucose goals for EVERY one: fasting < 5.3 · 1 h after meals < 7.8 mmol/L

groups.title: Found at 24–28 weeks: SCREEN every pregnancy

pres.title: Screen in order
lines: 1 · 50 g glucose, any time of day, 1 h: < 7.8 normal, stop · ≥ 11.1 = gestational diabetes (GDM)
2 · 7.8–11.0 → FASTING 75 g test: GDM if ANY of fasting ≥ 5.3, 1 h ≥ 10.6, 2 h ≥ 9.0

head: h
Before conception
the glycated hemoglobin (A1c) at conception sets the malformation risk
risk: • heart: transposition, coarctation, atrial septal defect
• gut atresias · kidney agenesis, double ureters
tx: • blood pressure drugs safe for a baby: see the HYPERTENSION IN PREGNANCY chart

head: h
Pregnant with type 1 or 2
follow closely: endocrinology + obstetrics (timing of delivery)
inv: 2 · Eyes: during + within a year after

head: h
Gestational diabetes (GDM)
weight + placental hormones → insulin resistance
risk: • baby > 4 kg: shoulder dystocia, brachial plexus injury
tx: • 3 meals of 45 g, 3 snacks of 20 g carbohydrate
• glyburide crosses the placenta: newborn lows

head: h
It was TYPE 2 all along
less often early type 1
risk: glucose or insulin doses unusually HIGH
inv: Glucose does NOT return to normal
on the 75 g test after delivery
